name: Emery Gordon
life: “My wife and I painted theater flats in a room too narrow to lay them down.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Emery by a small Wednesday habit. Emery checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I bid because there is a second menu under the first. My wife painted it on our honeymoon.
appearance: Emery has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for a neat white crop. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a rust-colored canvas coat with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. In conversation Emery squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Emery has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Emery's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To recover the older painted menu without damaging the top one.
family: Lucia Byrd is Emery’s younger cousin. Emery leaves the first voice message. Lucia calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A room above the dryers*, Lucia says, “I am the worker's partner. I can give up the kitchen table for art but I cannot give up part of the rent for a studio.”
connections: Levi Lucas. They document the hidden menu and credit the original chalk writing.

reactions.situation: A buyer offers to erase the board and repaint it
reactions.response: Emery asks the former owner to record the board before the paint is changed.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Emery stays beside the bystander in a public place and reports only what happened in sight and earshot.

reactions.response: Emery seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
reactions.asWritten: If the joke lands badly, Emery seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
